digest.component_or_area: CI workflows and Git fetch optimization
propositions: CI tickets-branch fetch operations transfer excessive data (1.04 GiB–6.73 minutes baseline) due to full blob history; applying --filter=blob:none reduces transfer to 68.7 MiB–22 MB and time to 14.3 s–8.6 s.

actions/checkout@v7 filter input and explicit --filter=blob:none flags must be added to named-origin and direct-URL git fetch paths while preserving fetch-depth: 0, depth semantics, and existing credentials/refs.
Production guards must enforce pack-size limits (102400 KiB standalone, 131072 KiB Gerrit) immediately after materialization and reject unfiltered fetches that exceed thresholds.

Git protocol must advertise filter capability, negotiate blob:none with server, and leave large historical blobs missing pre-materialization; git worktree materialization may fetch tip blobs but identity scanning must not add promisor objects.

A real-Git fixture using git daemon with GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL, packet-trace validation, and exact threshold repositories must prove the filter protocol, pack-size contracts, and no-promisor-fetch invariants.
Standalone and Gerrit verify-identity jobs must snapshot git count-objects before and after materialization to confirm identity scanning does not introduce new objects.
